Subject: Lumenica — contract sequencing and MAP items

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the team was impressed with the latency and the Dedicated capacity options. Procurement asked me to consolidate the sequence for legal signoff so we can align internal stakeholders. Quick asks from our side: 

- We need a single Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that ties the MSA, DPA, and the initial order form milestones to acceptance/testing windows. Can you provide a MAP template with ownership columns?
- Lumenica's security team wants to confirm DPA redlines can be tracked separately so signature of the MSA doesn't block data transfer testing. Is that possible?
- Procurement prefers a clear pull-through schedule: Order form signed -> POC window -> Production onboarding. Can you propose an end-to-end timeline and who at Redwood will own each gate?

If you can share a draft MAP and a proposed sprint for the close, we can review with legal and procurement end of week.

Thanks,
Emily

Hi Emily — thanks, and glad the demo landed well. Per your asks below, I pulled together a lightweight plan to avoid blocking testing on DPA redlines while legal works through details. See the attached MAP and a one-page manifest. High level: 

1) MAP (attached: Lumenica_MAP_v1.xlsx) — columns: milestone, owner (Redwood / Lumenica), dependency (MSA / DPA / Order Form), target date, acceptance criteria, fallbacks.

2) DPA handling — we can decouple operational data-transfer testing from DPA signature using a scoped "data-test" NDA + a limited SFTP/token access during POC. Legal can sign a DPA addendum once redlines are agreed; that will be tracked as a blocking flag in the MAP but won't prevent POC for non-production data.

3) Proposed sprint (dates are draft):
- Day 0 (Order form executed): commercial terms locked, billing cadence confirmed. Owner: Lumenica procurement + Redwood finance (Marcus).
- Day 1–14: POC and data-transfer tests using scoped test access. Owner: Lumenica engineering + Redwood solutions (Karthik).
- Day 15–30: Production enablement, final infra config, token rotation, and go/no-go. Owner: Redwood ops + Lumenica infra.

Please note any absolute blockers from procurement/legal and we'll surface escalation paths. I'm copying Karthik and Marcus who will own technical runbooks and billing/finance respectively.

Next steps I propose: 
- Marcus to confirm billing terms and change-of-service lead time by EOD Wed.
- Karthik to draft the POC runbook and test access checklist by Thu.
- Emily / Rajiv to confirm whether the scoped test NDA is acceptable to Lumenica legal (if yes, we'll route the minimal doc).

Attaching the MAP and manifest now.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
(attachment: Lumenica_MAP_v1.xlsx, attachment: MAP_manifest_onepager.pdf)

Laura / Karthik — thanks for the quick turn. A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal: 

- We need explicit language about data scope for the "data-test" NDA (time-bound, IP/retention carveouts). Lumenica legal prefers a separate DPA redline path but will accept a scoped NDA for non-production testing if the MAP shows the DPA milestone as required before production ramp.
- Billing: we require invoicing on a monthly calendar with a 30-day net term. Any changes to resource commitments during the POC must be captured as change orders on the order form.
- Can Redwood commit to a rollback plan if POC data shows unacceptable privacy leakage? We need a short procedural doc.

We reviewed the MAP manifest and added inline comments (see attached DPA_redlines_20260826.pdf). Would appreciate a consolidated response to comments and a proposal for who at Redwood signs the order form (name/title).

Thanks,
Rajiv Menon

Hi Rajiv / Emily — appreciate the notes. Below are concrete responses and a proposed binding sprint schedule so your stakeholders can calendar commitments.

Responses to legal/procurement points:
- Scoped test NDA: Redwood can sign a time-boxed, scoped NDA limited to test datasets (90 days max) that includes specific retention and access controls. We'll include an explicit clause that the scoped NDA does not replace the DPA; the DPA remains a production gating milestone in the MAP.
- Billing cadence: Marcus will own the order form's billing section. We accept monthly invoicing with Net 30; Marcus will confirm the billing contact and sample invoice by EOD Thu.
- Rollback plan: attached is a one-page rollback playbook (excerpt in MAP_manifest). Key points: immediate token revocation, data egress audit, and a freeze on model tuning. We can expand to a 2–3 page SOP if preferred.

Proposed binding sprint (finalized timeline):
- T+0 (Order form signature): Parties sign order form (Redwood signatory: Marcus Lin, Head of Finance).
- T+1–10: Scoped test NDA executed; test access provisioned (Redwood solutions + Lumenica infra).
- T+11–24: POC data transfer & functional validation. Acceptance criteria: end-to-end transfer, sample-run latency within SLA, no PII leakage in sample set.
- T+25–40: DPA execution window + production onboarding. DPA must be agreed for production traffic; if DPA is not finalized by T+40, we will hold production enablement and revert to scoped test environment.

Owners: 
- Redwood commercial / order sign: Marcus Lin (marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com)
- Redwood technical runbook & test access: Karthik Iyer (karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com)
- Redwood ops / production enablement: Laura Bennett

Next steps: 
1) Laura: we'll push an updated MAP that incorporates Rajiv's inline comments and embeds the rollback playbook.
2) Marcus: will send the sample invoice and confirm Redwood signatory details by EOD (Thu).
3) Emily / Rajiv: please confirm acceptance of the scoped NDA approach; if yes, we'll circulate the NDA for signature and provision test credentials.

I'll attach the short rollback playbook and a redlined MAP in the next message.

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
